channel.title: The PHP Dictionary — Recent Changes
channel.description: Recently added or updated entries in the PHP Dictionary.

item.title: Lint, Won't Execute
item.description: ``Lint, won't execute`` is a special state of the code, where the source can be parsed, but cannot be executed.

item.title: Capture The Flag (CTF)
item.description: Capture The Flag, abbreviated CTF, is a type of cybersecurity competition in which participants solve security challenges to find hidden strings called flags.

item.title: UUencode Encoding
item.description: Uuencode, short for ``Unix-to-Unix encoding``, is a binary-to-text encoding mechanism originally designed to transfer binary data over mediums that only support text, such as email or newsgroups.

item.title: Unicode
item.description: Unicode is a standard to represent text.

item.title: Try-catch
item.description: Try-catch is a PHP command, which runs a block of code, and catches some configured exceptions that the block may throw.

item.title: throw
item.description: Throw is the keyword which raises an exception.

item.title: Tabulation
item.description: A tabulation is a whitespace character, that often represents the equivalent of four space characters.

item.title: Resource Leak
item.description: A resource leak occurs when a resource, such as a file handle, database connection, network socket, or stream, is opened but never properly closed.

item.title: POSIX
item.description: ``posix`` is a PHP extension that gives access to functions defined in the IEEE 1003.

item.title: json_encode()
item.description: ``json_encode()`` encodes a data structure into a JSON string.

item.title: Ignored Catch
item.description: ``catch`` does not check that the caught exception exists.

item.title: Finally
item.description: Finally is the default clause of a try-catch expression.

item.title: Fatal Error
item.description: Fatal error is a type of PHP error, which ends the execution of the application.

item.title: Exception
item.description: Exceptions are a mechanism for handling errors and exceptional situations in a more structured and controlled way compared to traditional error handling methods like using error codes or ``die()`` statements.

item.title: Exception Handler
item.description: The exception handler is a default or custom function, which is called once an exception has exhausted all available ``try-catch`` blocks.

item.title: disable_functions
item.description: The ``disable_functions`` PHP directive prevents specific native functions from being called by the code.

item.title: Data Mapper
item.description: A data mapper, also called an object mapper, performs a bidirectional conversion of data, between PHP's OOP representation and a database storage.

item.title: Catchable Fatal Error
item.description: A catchable fatal error is a fatal error that PHP allows user code to intercept before the script terminates, instead of stopping execution unconditionally.

item.title: Catch
item.description: ``catch`` is the complement clause of try.

item.title: Argon2
item.description: Argon2 is a modern, secure, and highly efficient password hashing algorithm.

item.title: Anonymous Catch
item.description: Traditionally, the catch statement requires specifying both an Exception class and an identifier variable to hold the caught exception.

item.title: Interface Segregation Principle (ISP)
item.description: The interface segregation principle, or ISP, states that no code should be forced to depend on methods it does not use.

item.title: JavaScript Object Notation (JSON)
item.description: ``JSON``, or JavaScript Object Notation, is a lightweight data-interchange format.

item.title: JSON Lines (JSONC)
item.description: ``JSONC``, aka SON with Comments, is a superset of JSON that extends its functionality by allowing single-line ``//`` and multi-line ``/* */`` comments.

item.title: JSON Lines (JSONL)
item.description: JSONL, JSON Lines, is a text-based format where each line is a valid, independent JSON object, separated by newline characters.

item.title: Software Bill Of Material (SBOM)
item.description: A Software Bill of Materials, aka ``SBOM``, is a formal, machine-readable inventory of all components, libraries, and dependencies used in a software project.

item.title: Static Code Analysis (SCA)
item.description: Static code analysis, or ``SCA`` or static analysis, analyzes the source code:

item.title: Software Development Kit (SDK)
item.description: SDK stands for Software Development Kit.

item.title: Search Engine
item.description: A search engine is a system that indexes and retrieves data based on queries.

item.title: Search Engine Optimization (SEO)
item.description: Search Engine Optimization, or SEO, is the practice of improving a website so that search engines rank it higher in search results.

item.title: serialize_precision
item.description: The ``serialize_precision`` directive controls the number of significant digits used when serializing float values via ``serialize()`` and ``json_encode()``.

item.title: Serverless
item.description: Serverless computing is an execution model where a cloud provider allocates compute resources on demand, scaling to zero when idle.

item.title: Service Registry
item.description: A service registry is a database of available service instances in a distributed system.

item.title: Sqids
item.description: ``Sqids``, formerly known as ``Hashids``, is an open-source library that encodes one or more non-negative integers into short, YouTube-like alphanumeric strings, and decodes them back.

item.title: SQL Database
item.description: A SQL database is a database server that processes data based on the SQL language.

item.title: Contract Test
item.description: A contract test checks that two sides of an interface agree on the messages they exchange.

item.title: Authorization Header
item.description: The Authorization header carries the credentials that a client sends to a server to authenticate a request.

item.title: Mocking
item.description: Mocking is the practice of replacing a dependency with a controlled object during a test.

item.title: Mock
item.description: A mock replaces a code dependency with an object, to make testing easier.

item.title: Malformed Response Body
item.description: A malformed response body is an HTTP response whose content does not match what the client expects.

item.title: json_decode()
item.description: ``json_decode()`` decodes a JSON string into a data structure.

item.title: Application Programming Interface (API)
item.description: An API is a set of functions and procedures allowing the creation of applications that access the features or data of another service.

item.title: Fixture
item.description: A fixture is a set of test data.

item.title: HTTP Code
item.description: HTTP status codes are three-digit numeric codes that are returned by web servers to indicate the outcome of a client's request to a server.

item.title: HTTP Headers
item.description: HTTP headers are extra information, exchanged between the server and the client, to configure further the network transaction.

item.title: Integration Test
item.description: Integration tests are tests that verify how multiple components or packages work together, as opposed to unit tests, where test are dedicated to one component.

item.title: Properties
item.description: Class properties are variables, local to an object or a class.

item.title: Retry
item.description: A retry is the act of re-attempting an operation that previously failed, typically due to a transient error such as a network timeout, a temporarily unavailable service, or a rate-limit response.

item.title: Supply Chain Attack
item.description: Supply Chain Attack is a security attack that uses dependencies to infect a program.
